deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). X = P^1(C) minus {0,1,∞}. Its fundamental group π is free on the loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ subject to l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. Γ = Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2 is the group of holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms of P^1 preserving {0,1,∞}; ε̇ denotes the generator of Z/2, complex conjugation. Σ is the orbifold fundamental group of X/Γ, an extension 1 → π → Σ → Γ → 1. In modern terms, with π ≅ Γ(2)/±1, Σ is the extended modular group PGL_2(Z) and its holomorphic part is PSL_2(Z). This is the (2,3,∞) triangle group.

Formula block (10). It is a presentation (the last stage of an older computation) with generators ρ and ε_0, ε_1, ε_∞:
- ρ^3 = 1, with ρ lying over the 3-cycle;
- ε_∞^2 ε_1^2 ε_0^2 = 1, which reads as the fundamental relation l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1 if ε_i^2 corresponds to l_i;
- three cyclically permuted relations expressing each ε_i through the others and ρ.
The marginal note says one should at least write the conjugation relations ρ ε_0 ρ^{-1} = ε_1, etc., and so present the group on (ε_0, ρ) alone. Grothendieck then asks whether ρ can be expressed in the ε_i and says that, 'as before', it cannot.

Main argument. One wants to lift the elements of Γ (in particular ε̇) to Σ. No lift is privileged: there are three equally natural choices. Instead he takes the isotropy subgroup in Γ of a point P. From the condition this is P = e^{iπ/3} (and ρ̄ = e^{-iπ/3} is its conjugate). Its stabiliser consists of the pairs (σ̇, ε̇^{sg σ̇}):
- even permutations act holomorphically (rotations of order 3 about P);
- odd permutations are composed with conjugation (e.g. z ↦ 1/z̄, which fixes the unit circle through P).
This gives the embedding (11) φ: S_3 → S_3 × Z/2, σ ↦ (σ, sgn σ). Because P is a point fixed by this group, the isotropy group lifts canonically into the orbifold fundamental group, giving the section (12) σ ↦ σ̃: S_3 → Σ.

One sets σ̃_i to be the lifts of the three transpositions; these are the three reflections through P, and ρ̃ = ρ. The previous page then derives σ̃_i^2 = 1 and σ̃_0σ̃_1 = σ̃_1σ̃_∞ = σ̃_∞σ̃_0 = ρ, together with the action of the σ̃_i on the l_i. The next page forms τ_i = σ_i σ̃_i, identifies the Malgoire–Voisin bicoloured cartographic group Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 (its even part is π), and passes to profinite completions and Autext_lac(π̂), i.e. towards the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting.

Purpose. The page produces explicit, symmetric (S_3-equivariant) presentations of Σ ≅ PGL_2(Z) adapted to the action of Γ_{0,3}. These serve as preparation for describing the outer action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points) together with its S_3 × Z/2 symmetries.
errors: The claim 'ρ ne s'exprime pas en fonction des ε_i' is doubtful under the natural reading. If the ε_i lie over the transpositions (holomorphic or composed with conjugation) and their squares give the l_i, then H = <ε_i> contains π and maps onto a subgroup of Γ containing the image of ρ, so ρ ∈ H. Concretely, in PSL_2(Z) the parabolics T and U generate everything: S = T^{-1} U T^{-1}, so ST, of order 3, lies in <T, U>. The claim can only hold if the ε_i are something else, e.g. if ε_i^2 does not generate π. The meaning of ε_i is defined on earlier pages not shown, so this is flagged rather than asserted.

The last three lines of (10) are only partly legible and cannot be checked as written. They look like a garbled attempt to encode conjugation by ρ, which the marginal note itself criticises ('il faudrait écrire (au moins!) les relations ρε_0ρ^{-1}=ε_1').
This is a superseded draft ('vieille rédaction'). The approach via ε_i is abandoned on this very page in favour of the isotropy-group lifts σ̃_i.

ideas.what: Σ = orbifold π_1 of (P^1 − {0,1,∞}) / (S_3 × Z/2), as an extension of Γ_{0,3} by the free group π
ideas.modern_name: extended modular group PGL_2(Z) ⊃ PSL_2(Z) ⊃ Γ(2)/±1; (2,3,∞) triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); in the dessins context Grothendieck, Malgoire–Voisin, Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, PSL_2(Z)/PGL_2(Z), Γ_{0,3}), 1984

ideas.what: Canonical S_3-equivariant lift of the stabiliser of the point e^{iπ/3} in S_3×Z/2, embedded as σ ↦ (σ, sgn σ), giving three reflections σ̃_i with σ̃_iσ̃_j = ρ
ideas.modern_name: isotropy (local) group at an orbifold point as a canonical base point; reflection presentation of PGL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical reflection-group theory; base-point issues for π_1(P^1−3 pts) treated with tangential base points by Deligne and Ihara

ideas.what: Presentation (10) with generators ρ and ε_i, and the question of whether ρ is redundant
ideas.modern_name: Tietze manipulation of a presentation of PSL_2(Z)/PGL_2(Z)

ideas.what: Link (on the neighbouring pages) to the Malgoire–Voisin cartographic group and to Autext_lac(π̂)

missed.claim: Choosing the symmetric orbifold point e^{iπ/3}, whose stabiliser in Γ_{0,3} is S_3 embedded via σ ↦ (σ, sgn σ), gives a canonical S_3-equivariant base point for π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) together with its real structure. This is an alternative to tangential base points. It is a minor technical device and is essentially implicit in the classical triangle-group picture.
missed.quote: il paraît plus commode de considérer le sous-groupe d'isotropie de P dans Γ=Γ_{03}=S_3×Z/2 ... qui se relèvent canoniquement en des éléments de Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: At most minor. Symmetric base points are relevant to writing S_3 × Z/2-symmetric versions of the GT relations, but the idea is standard in spirit.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft computation of standard presentations of PGL_2(Z) as the orbifold π_1 of P^1 minus three points modulo S_3 × Z/2. The content is classical and the overall programme is published in the Esquisse. Its one non-routine assertion, that ρ is not expressible in the ε_i, appears dubious, and nothing here seems new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The '9' at the top right is the page number of the old draft, not part of the formulas.

The last three lines of (10) are uncertain. The factors after ρ (read as 'ε_0^2 [?]') contain heavily overwritten symbols, possibly ρ^{±1}, so they may encode conjugation by ρ. The exponents '4' are also uncertain.
The marginal note reads roughly: 'il faudrait écrire (au moins!) les relations ρ ε_0 ρ^{-1} = ε_1 etc. dans [en fonction de] (ε_0, ρ)'.
In 'les couples σ̇, ε̇^{ε} tels que sg(σ̇) = ε', ε denotes ±1, i.e. the pairs (σ̇, ε̇^{sg σ̇}).
On the next page, 'Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/12' should almost certainly be S_3 × Z/2, consistent with this page. Likewise 'image inverse de Z/12 engendré par τ' should read Z/2.
